chunks: 2. Al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿUbayd Allah informed me, from a number of our companions, from Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ḥammād, from Ḥarīz, from Ibn Muslim, who said:

I said to Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام: A man urinated and did not have water with him. He said: He should squeeze the base of his penis to the tip three squeezes, and shake its end; then if something comes out after that, it is not urine, but rather it is from the passages.
3. As for what al-Ṣaffār narrated from Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, who said: A man wrote to him:
Is wudu (ablution) required because of what comes out from the penis after istibrāʾ? So he wrote: Yes.

The correct approach regarding it is that we interpret it as indicating a kind of recommendation rather than obligation, or we interpret it as a case of taqiyyah, because it accords with the doctrine of most of the general populace.

key_terms.التَّقِيَّةِ: taqiyyah, dissimulation or precautionary conformity under particular circumstances
key_terms.الذَّكَرِ: the penis, the organ from which discharge is discussed
key_terms.الِاسْتِبْرَاءِ: istibrāʾ, the procedure performed after urination to clear remaining moisture
key_terms.الِاسْتِحْبَابِ: recommendation, meaning non-obligatory preference in law
key_terms.الْبَوْلِ: urine, whose legal ruling is being distinguished from later moisture
key_terms.الْحَبَائِلِ: the passages/channels, referring here to non-urine moisture
key_terms.الْوُضُوءُ: wudu (ablution), the ritual purification discussed as possibly required

ai.seo_question: Is wudu (ablution) required if something comes out after istibrāʾ following urination?
ai.summary: This report discusses the ruling of istibrāʾ after urination and the legal status of moisture emerging afterward. It indicates that after performing the prescribed squeezing and shaking, what exits subsequently is not treated as urine, while another report requiring wudu (ablution) is understood as recommendation or as issued under taqiyyah.
